SMTO-EXE-0009 — SMTO can't run this command with administrator rights here

GUID: a9e17be6-31b8-41e4-993a-37f0374c6f23
Slug: privilege-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • The command needed administrator (sudo) rights, but the chosen computer, or the way the command was set to run, doesn't allow that. The command didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Execution target menu and check which Gateway the task used. Administrator commands only work on Linux or macOS computers where the sudo program is installed. If that computer runs Windows or lacks sudo, SMTO has no way to raise permissions there.
  2. If the command expects you to type answers or use a live terminal, ask SMTO to run it without prompts, for example by giving the answers in your request. Administrator commands must run without interaction so SMTO can pass your password safely.
  3. Once the target or the request is corrected, ask SMTO to run the command again. The command never started, so running it again won't repeat anything.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and shows its output in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway; they may need to install sudo or update the Gateway. Only give your administrator password when SMTO asks for it during the task, never in other messages.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Privileged execution was refused before launch because the target cannot elevate (non-POSIX OS, sudo not installed, or the client/Gateway lacks a privileged endpoint) or the request mode is incompatible (privileged runs require a captured, non-interactive shell_command with no stdin).

What this means

  • Privileged execution is unavailable for the OS, missing sudo or Gateway method/endpoint, or incompatible with the request's stdin, interaction or execution mode. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Privileged execution is unavailable for the OS, missing sudo or Gateway method/endpoint, or incompatible with the request's stdin, interaction or execution mode.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect platform, advertised privilege support, executable availability and captured/noninteractive request constraints.

How to fix it

  • Check the receipt error_kind (privilege_unavailable or remote_privilege_unavailable) and stderr. Use a POSIX Gateway with sudo on PATH and a client exposing the privileged stream endpoint, submit a shell_command with execution_mode=captured, interaction_mode=non_interactive and stdin_mode=none (use background=true jobs and command-owned heredocs for input), and supply credentials only through the private credential flow.
  • Use a supported privileged execution route and request mode on the intended target. Supply credentials only through the existing private flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported authorized privilege route accepts the exact request form and reports an elevation result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
